title: Payoff and Loan Satisfaction Worksheet: Retention Daily Accrual
content:
# Retention daily accrual worksheet — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction

On the payoff case of a Borrower Voluntary Payoff requested by the borrower of record on a loan whose maturity case is due and payable, in its extension period or referred to foreclosure, the retention daily accrual is the retention accrual basis times the loan's daily accrual rate, rounded half up to the cent and only at that last step.

**Line 1 — daily accrual rate.** The loan's note rate (percent) plus, for a HECM, the annual MIP rate (percent) of its payout plan, divided by 100 and by the plan's per diem day count. A Summit loan carries no MIP, so its rate is its note rate alone. The rate is not rounded.

**Line 2 — retention accrual basis.** The loan's principal balance plus five carried advances: the set-aside disbursement carry, the preservation advance carry, the due-and-payable appraisal carry, the replacement appraisal carry and the foreclosure charge carry.

**Line 3 — carried advances.** The set-aside disbursement carry, the preservation advance carry, the replacement appraisal carry and the foreclosure charge carry are each 0.00, and the due-and-payable appraisal carry is USD 475.00.

**Line 4 — result.** Line 2 times line 1, rounded half up to the cent; nothing is rounded before this line.

### Worked example on hypothetical inputs

| Hypothetical input | Value |
|---|---|
| Loan | HECM |
| Principal balance | USD 200000.00 |
| Note rate | 6.5 percent |
| Annual MIP rate of the payout plan | 0.5 percent |
| Per diem day count | 365 |

- Daily accrual rate: 6.5 plus 0.5 is 7.0 percent; divided by 100 and by 365, about 0.000191781 per day.
- Retention accrual basis: USD 200000.00 plus 0.00, 0.00, USD 475.00, 0.00 and 0.00, so USD 200475.00.
- Retention daily accrual: USD 200475.00 times the daily rate is USD 38.4473 before rounding, USD 38.45 after.

For a hypothetical Summit loan with the same balance and a note rate of 7.0 percent, the rate and the result are the same, since no MIP is added. The inputs are invented for the illustration and describe no loan.
